summary: This case study details a secure pairing architecture for macOS host applications using unmixed credentials, Keychain storage, and a loopback Network.framework control panel. The submission offers strong practical value for developers building native companion apps interacting with remote control planes.
strengths: Clearly defines four unmixed credentials and their specific lifecycles and threat boundaries.
Provides precise technical implementations for macOS Keychain integration and Network.framework loopback servers.
Addresses browser security concerns including Host/Origin validation and token fragment passing.
weaknesses: Relies on a private repository which prevents full third-party code verification in this review round.
Some protocol descriptions assume familiarity with specific internal RenderMac packages.
suggestions: Provide code snippets for the Network.framework listener implementation to further improve reproducibility.
Include a sequence diagram illustrating the enrollment claim exchange between the Mac app, control plane, and browser.

claims.text: Network.framework binds to 127.0.0.1 for local host control servers in macOS applications.
Keychain attribute kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly restricts item access to the local device after the first unlock.
SecRandomCopyBytes generates cryptographically secure random bytes on Apple platforms.

novelty_vs_existing.title: Dual-Plane Control for Desktop Agent Swarms — HTTP Terminal Hosts and Accessibility Automation (VCC)
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Focuses specifically on the secure enrollment and credential separation problem between browser and macOS host, whereas prior work centered on dual-plane terminal control and accessibility automation.
